## T-778 — Six more register-at-mount thread_local seams have no lifecycle guard — port the wave-129 idiom

- **Slice spec:** ``
- **Program hub:** ``
- **Branch:** `ticket/T-778`
- **Targets:** website
- **Summary:** MAJOR, found during wave 129's fix pass and filed rather than fixed because it spans four files outside that wave's owns. THE DEFECT SHAPE, proven twice in wave 129: a `thread_local` seam registered when a component mounts and never unregistered stays callable after the component dies. Backspace hide-chrome unmounts panels (mission_editor.rs, NO modal guard, and dialogs explicitly survive the hide), after which the stale closure REPORTS SUCCESS -- `true`, or a stale value -- while every `set` writes to DISPOSED signals, which reactive_graph 0.2.14 makes a SILENT NO-OP. A click reports success and does nothing: a dead click by lifecycle rather than by routing. TWO FAILURE MODES, and a naive fix closes only the first: (1) no unregister at all, so the stale hook answers forever; (2) an UNCONDITIONAL unregister, so a REMOUNT that installs before the dead component's cleanup runs is clobbered by that cleanup. VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-08-08, `grep -c` per file -- each has register-at-mount seams and ZERO `ptr_eq` and ZERO `on_cleanup`: apps/website/frontend/src/ruler_tool.rs (RULER_CHAIN, 1 seam); apps/website/frontend/src/los_tool.rs (LOS_STATE, LOS_SAMPLER, VIEWSHED_STATE, 3 seams); apps/website/frontend/src/world_assets/mod.rs (register_render_ctx, 1 seam); apps/website/frontend/src/select_tool.rs (register_editor_selection, 1 seam -- this one is DOCUMENTED as deliberately leaking with the engine, so confirm the intent before changing it rather than assuming). THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND SHIPPED TWICE -- port it, do not re-invent: `install_seam`/`unregister_seam` plus the `SeamRegistration` trait at apps/website/frontend/src/validation_panel.rs (wave 129, dac84b03) is the generic form covering four seams; eden_dock_right.rs's `install_select_zone` (f6a2b687) is the single-seam form. Register + `on_cleanup` unregister guarded by `Rc::ptr_eq` so only the LOSING registration is cleared. `on_cleanup` is Send + Sync-bound and `Rc<dyn Fn>` is !Send, so park the Rc in a `StoredValue::new_local` and read it back inside the cleanup -- cleanups run BEFORE arena nodes are removed, so the read is valid, and holding the clone keeps the allocation alive. DO NOT compare a bare `usize` address: the old Rc drops on re-register, so a later hook can be allocated at the freed address and a stale cleanup would wrongly clear it (ABA). For a signal-valued seam use the arena key `==` (slotmap versions its keys, so a recycled slot is not mistaken for its predecessor). ACCEPTANCE, three behavioural cases per seam, as wave 129 pinned them: install -> cleanup -> the read reports honest failure AND the stale hook is not called at all; install(A) -> install(B) -> A's cleanup -> B SURVIVES and still answers; never-installed -> honest failure. Perturb both ways: removing the cleanup must redden case 1, and removing the ptr_eq guard must redden case 2 ALONE -- case 2 is the one a naive fix gets wrong. WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: in wave 129 a fix agent ADDED a new instance of this defect (validation_panel.rs `register_route_probe`) while a sibling agent was fixing the identical shape twelve lines away, and then made row clickability depend on it. The pattern is easy to get wrong and there was no shared idiom; now there is one. Audit every seam you touch and every seam you add.

## T-779 — set_loadout discards the acknowledgement T-770 added, so the history tail fires over writes that never happened

- **Slice spec:** ``
- **Program hub:** ``
- **Branch:** `ticket/T-779`
- **Targets:** website
- **Summary:** RESIDUE of T-770 (wave 140), verified by the orchestrator 2026-08-08. T-770's whole point was that `commit_writes` counted closure CALLS rather than sink acknowledgements, so its WARNING arm was unreachable. The core half landed: `MissionDocCore::update_slot_loadout` (crates/map-engine-core/src/doc/store.rs:2784) now returns `bool` and returns `false` when the slot id is not in the document. THE FRONTEND HALF DID NOT. `editor_ops::set_loadout` (apps/website/frontend/src/editor_ops.rs:2005) calls `core.update_slot_loadout(id, loadout_json);` and then hardcodes `true` as the value of `did`, discarding the acknowledgement entirely. CONSEQUENCES, both live: (1) `crate::mission_history::after_local_edit()` fires whenever the OPS_CTX and doc merely EXIST, so a set_loadout against a stale or deleted slot id still marks the mission dirty and mints an undo step over a document that did not change; (2) any receipt built on this path still cannot distinguish a real write from a no-op, which is precisely the defect T-770 was filed to close. FIX: return the mutator's bool out of the closure instead of `true`, so `did` means what its name says, and gate `after_local_edit()` on it. Then check the callers — `arsenal.rs:1253` is the live one — and decide whether a refused write should surface to the operator rather than passing silently. ACCEPTANCE: a test that calls set_loadout with an id that is NOT in the document and asserts no history entry is minted and the mission is not dirtied; perturb by restoring the hardcoded `true` and watch it go red. Note arsenal.rs carries source pins naming `pub fn set_loadout` and its tail line (arsenal.rs:6180, :6205, :4897) — update them honestly, do not delete them.

T-768 delivered the connect gesture's pointer half once T-723 fixed the armed-pointerup path, so a connection can now be STARTED and FINISHED on the map. What it did not deliver is a rendered LINE: connections draw nothing, so there is no artifact to click, and CONN-DEL-001 (delete a connection) is reachable only from the panel's Delete control. RECIPE: add the connection lane to draw_order.rs and engine.rs the way the marker lane was added by T-760; feed it from the document, NOT from a slice's own owns — T-069 and T-672 independently established that a lane fed from a slice's own state goes stale after undo/redo/restore, which is why the feed comes first; then wire pick/hit-testing so a line can be selected, and route Delete through the existing path rather than authoring a second one. ACCEPTANCE: draw a connection, undo, redo, restore from IDB, and confirm the line survives each; then select the line on the map and delete it through the same code path the panel's Delete uses.
